changes.location: Security Signal Review > Identity and Access
changes.before: ## Endpoint and Vulnerabilities
changes.after:
In Q3, authentication coverage declined from Q2 even though Identity remained the highest-scoring category at 81.7%, so the category score should not be read as evidence of uniform protection. ASM should validate the account-type and enforcement context, confirm privileged-account coverage and documented exclusions, and review service accounts for a more secure form of authentication. These actions address the continuing MFA and SSPR gaps and support a proportionate response to the credential-based risk described above.

observations.detail: The draft refers to "AMS’s overall Secure Score" while the client is named ASM everywhere else. Left as drafted under the substance-freeze rule.

observations.location: Security Signal Review > Identity and Access
observations.detail: The first Identity paragraph ended with an unfinished fragment ("ASM’s identity secure"). The fragment asserted no fact and was removed; confirm nothing substantive was intended.

observations.location: Security Signal Review > Data Protection and Collaboration > Mailbox auditing 0/3 row
observations.detail: The Assessment interpretation for Mailbox auditing 0/3 repeats the sensitivity-label and forwarding recommendation instead of addressing mailbox auditing. Left unchanged.

observations.location: Recommended Security Actions > CIS Microsoft 365 Foundation Benchmark
observations.detail: The Status cells for the "Review labels and forwarding" and "Validate mailbox audit completeness" rows repeat theme and recommendation text that does not describe the status of those items. Left unchanged.

observations.location: Security Signal Review > control evidence tables
observations.detail: The draft used the internal classification labels "Regressed since Q2" and "Improved since Q2" as stand-alone table text. They were restated as complete sentences ("The control regressed since Q2.") with the same meaning because the template has no such label convention.

observations.location: Recommended Security Actions > Active Recommendations and CIS tables
observations.detail: The template requires status entries in the form MM.DD.YYYY - <STATUS DESCRIPTION>. The draft supplies no per-item dates, so the draft status wording was retained.

observations.location: Recommended Security Actions > Active Recommendations and CIS tables
observations.detail: The template shows bold recommendation titles. The draft recommendation titles are not bold, and no markdown formatting was added.

observations.location: Security Signal Review > Identity, Data Protection, Cloud Workload and AI sections
observations.detail: The template includes supporting screenshot placeholders for these sections and a trendline screenshot under Control Movement. The draft contains only the Secure Score screenshot and the Defender exposure distribution screenshot, so no other images were added.
Several draft tables carry an empty header row ahead of the real header row, and some table bodies are split from their header by a blank line. The structure was frozen as drafted.
